Punjabi, slide 1: the pin made the piece ਫਸ, the same word 4.10 uses for “trapped”, two ideas the level teaches as different. Now ਮੋਹਰਾ ਜਕੜਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ.
Slide 2 now shows a position (2026-10-08): a bishop skewering the king to the queen behind it.

Chess bug, fixed in the app's rules: the Try accepted Nd6+ and Nf6+. After either one the queen just takes the checking knight, which also takes her off the rook's file, so White loses the knight for nothing. A moving piece may hang only when the UNCOVERED piece gives check; a check from the moving piece itself is no excuse. Now only the four safe knight moves count, and a test guards it.
Slide 2 now shows a position (2026-10-08): Ng6+ checks and uncovers the rook on the queen.
Punjabi, slide 2: ਆਪ ਵੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਮੋਹਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਖ਼ਤਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਕੋ ਵੇਲੇ ਦੋ ਖ਼ਤਰੇ!

Punjabi goal: ਜਿਤਾਉਂਦਾ / ਹਰਾਉਂਦਾ meant winning or losing the game. Now ਕਦੋਂ ਫ਼ਾਇਦਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਦੋਂ ਵਟਾਂਦਰਾ, ਅਤੇ ਕਦੋਂ ਘਾਟਾ.
English and Punjabi, the Try's answer: “White is a pawn and a knight up for a pawn” is now White gives one pawn and takes a pawn and a knight, so White wins a knight.
Punjabi, practice: clearer subjects and word order, and ਕੀ ਮਾਰਨਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ? for “Capture?” (a bare ਮਾਰੋ? read as an order).
